  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Senior Citizen Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed
to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit of
Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We will
be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  A. Regular meeting held May 22, 2023

SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits
any Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds
that a catastrophe or emergency exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and
need for action thereon) arose within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot (except as stated)
participate it is requested that all such communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda
for full discussion and action.

Any public member addressing the Board shall limit his or her address to three (3) minutes regarding the subject
under discussion. If a member of the public wishes to donate their time to another speaker, both persons must
be physically present and in attendance of the meeting. In no event shall any donations of time exceed six minutes
of total speaking time per person on any one item. The Presiding Officer may, in his or her discretion, extend the
3-minute time limitation for the particular subject under discussion for all speakers. In no event shall the total
amount of speaking time exceed 6 minutes per person for the subject under discussion. Organized group of
persons wishing to address the Board on the same subject matter, should select a spokesperson to represent the
group, so as to avoid unnecessary repetition. The Commission may regulate a speaker who is speaking too long,
being unduly repetitious, or extending discussion of irrelevancies.

In the hybrid format, both in-person and hybrid audience members will participate in the following order:
Tier 1: In-person attendees

Tier 2: Teleconference attendees

Tier 3: In-person and teleconference attendees who have not previously provide comments on the matter(s) being
discussed by the legislative body

5050 N. IRWINDALE AVENUE  MONDAY
IRWINDALE, CALIFORNIA 91706  9:00 A.M.

The Irwindale SENIOR CITIZEN COMMISSION met in regular session at the above time and place.

ROLL CALL:  Present: Commissioners Carol Acosta, Christina Fraijo,
  Patricia Gonzales; Vice Chair Iris Rodriguez; Chair Maggie Guzman

  Also present: Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Works Services Director;
  Eloise Beltran, Senior Center Manager; and Armando Hegdahl,
  Management Analyst

SPONTANEOUS
COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  A motion was made by Commissioner Gonzales, seconded by Chair
  Guzman, to approve the Consent Calendar. The motion was
  unanimously approved.

ITEM NO. 1A  MINUTES
MINUTES
  The minutes of the special meeting held April 24, 2023, were
  approved.

END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS  None.

SENIOR CENTER
MANAGER UPDATE  Senior Center Manager Beltran provided the following update:

  1) The following events were held in May: Loteria, Mothers’ Day Tea,
  and a Senior Art Festival.
  2) A Birthday Brunch will be held this Friday.
  3) Bingo will be held on Wednesday.
  4) Registrations for Irwindale classes begin today, and registrations for
  Mt. Sac classes begin on May 31.
  5) A Senior Center Parking Lot sale has been scheduled for June 3 and
  will feature a pancake fundraiser.
  6) The Senior Center Prom King and Queen will be announced at the
  Prom on June 23.
  7) A Father’s Day BBQ will be held on June 16 at the park.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE  Director Rodriguez provided the following update:

  1) Athens Services will be coordinating recycling and waste disposal
  activities at the Senior Center to help educate seniors on how to
  properly sort their waste.

  2) The 1st reading of the city budget will be held at a special City Council
  meeting scheduled for June 8.
  3) The June 14 City Council meeting has been cancelled.
  4) A compost and hazardous materials recycling event was held May 13.
  5) A “Saved by Skateboarding” event was also held May 13, in addition
  to the skateboard giveback event held at Jardin de Roca Park.
  6) The Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast held on June 16 featured pastors from
  various denominations that prayed for residents, the community, and
  first responders.
  7) An Aquatics Expo was held on Saturday.
  8) Arrow Highway from Avenida Barbosa to Live Oak will begin today.
  9) The Music in the Park concerts begin June 29.
  10) National Public Works Week will be celebrated this week.

COMMISSIONER ITEMS
AND REQUESTS

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Gonzales spoke highly of the trip to the LA County Fair
GONZALES  that the seniors enjoyed and thanked staff for the free meal vouchers they
  received. She also complimented staff for the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast
  event.

DIRECTOR RODRIGUEZ  In response to a question by Commissioner Gonzales, Director
  Rodriguez advised that the Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast event will likely be
  made into an annual event.

CHAIR GUZMAN  Chair Guzman spoke on the high turnout for the Bunco activities and
  thanked Senior Center staff, particularly new staffers that are working
  hard.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Gonzales thanked staff for the wonderful Mother’s Day
GONZALES  Tea event.

COMMISSIONER  Replying to a question by Commissioner Acosta, Manager Beltran
ACOSTA  indicated that the Senior Center submitted a budget request for the
  purchase of a new handicap van.

CHAIR GUZMAN  In response to a concern by Chair Guzman, Manager Beltran indicated
  that staff will be repairing the hinge of a door.

VICE CHAIR RODRIGUEZ Vice Chair Rodriguez spoke on the great success of the Mayor’s Prayer
  Breakfast function.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Gonzales noted that two seniors did not attend the trip to
GONZALES  the Fair, to which Director Rodriguez indicated that the City did not lose
  money on unused tickets for this function. However, staff will work toward
  attempting to change the public’s perception that it does not matter if
  individuals enroll to attend trips but think it is not a big deal to not show
  up since it did not cost them anything.
